newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore interest in Bangalore airport waning.
newsitem.headline: Singapore interest in Bangalore airport waning.

text.p: A Singapore consortium is likely to pull out of the Bangalore airport project following the Indian's government's revision of terms for the project, consortium sources said on Monday.
"We have put the project on hold for almost a year. There is likely to be a formal statement before the end of the week on where we stand," one source told Reuters.
"Basically, we are not agreeable to the new terms from the Indian government and we have told them that," he said.

The Singapore consortium comprises six companies -- L&M Group Investment, RSP Architects, Arcasia Land (formerly Technology Parks), Singapore Technologies, Sembawang Industrial and Parameswara Holdings.

The Indian partner in the Bangalore airport project is the Tata group with a 26 percent stake, U.S. company Raytheon with 24.5 percent and the Karnataka state government, whose capital is Bangalore, holds 25 percent.
The Singapore sources said the other partners in the project also found the revised terms for the Bangalore project unacceptable.
Karnataka had initially offered the Singapore $640 million project under conditions which would allow the consortium to build, own and operate (BOO) the airport.
But Indian Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim has insisted the project go ahead under a a build, own and transfer (BOT) scheme.
